info.name: eSignet mosipid - PMS client + e2e login
info.description:
Drives by hand the same path the api-test e2e surface drives: get an admin token, register an OIDC client through PMS, then run authorize -> flow/execute -> OTP -> consent against eSignet.

Run the requests in order. Each stores what the next needs (admin_token, client_id, execution_id, challenge_token), so after the first pass you can re-run folder 2 alone to repeat a login.

READ FIRST - a client you have just created will NOT work. IDA does not recognise a new OIDC client for somewhere between 20 minutes and 3 hours; until then every login dies at 'Send OTP' with IDA-MLC-007. Register a client once, leave it alone, and reuse its clientId from then on. The environment ships with an already-aged client so folder 2 works immediately.

The OTP is not automatable here: read it from the deployment's mock SMTP (https://smtp.<env>.mosip.net) and put it in the `otp` variable before running 2.5.

exec: // AUTH_PARTNER gates PMS /oidc-clients. Without it that call returns KER-ATH-403.
console.warn('No AUTH_PARTNER role - PMS /oidc-clients will return KER-ATH-403. Use /oauth/client instead, or grant the role.');
} catch (e) { console.log('could not decode token claims'); }

request.description: Client-credentials grant. The token goes to PMS as a COOKIE named Authorization, not a Bearer header - MOSIP kernel services answer KER-ATH-401 to the header form.

exec: if (code === 'KER-ATH-403') console.error('The token lacks the AUTH_PARTNER realm role.');
if (code === 'PMS_ESI_001') console.error('That modulus is already registered - put a NEW modulus in client_public_key_n.');
console.warn('Created ' + id + '. IDA will NOT accept it for 20 min to 3 h. Leave it, then set client_id to it.');

request.description:
Registers a client bound to an onboarded partner and a published policy.

Set client_public_jwk to a COMPLETE public JWK object, not just the modulus. Easiest source is https://mkjwk.org - RSA, 2048, Signature, RS256, Key ID SHA-256 - then copy the 'Public Key' panel (the right-hand one) and paste it whole. Keep the private half from the left panel if you intend to sign a private_key_jwt assertion at the token endpoint; the login flow in folder 2 does not need it, so a manual OTP test works without it.

The JWK should include kid. It is NOT what makes IDA accept the client - a client registered without kid authenticates fine - but the Go harness emits one (internal/e2e/crypto.go, publicJWK), so matching it keeps manual and automated clients comparable when you are diffing behaviour between them.

Every client needs its OWN modulus; reusing one gives PMS_ESI_001 'Client public key already exists'. PMS dedupes on n, not on kid, so re-pasting an old key under a new kid is still rejected.

If the client registers ACTIVE but every OTP attempt returns IDA-MLC-007, suspect the PMS->IDA websub delivery. That event is LOST rather than queued, so a client created while it is down is permanently unusable and waiting does not help - register a fresh one once it is healthy. A NEW client that works while an OLDER one still fails is the signature of that outage.

/oauth/client is an alternative endpoint needing no AUTH_PARTNER role.

Shows relyingPartyId, policyId, status, claims and acrValues.

Beware: two clients can look identical here and still behave differently at IDA, purely because one is older. This view cannot tell you whether IDA has picked a client up.
Confirms PMS pushed the client through to eSignet. Returns clientId and status only - and status here does NOT predict whether IDA will authenticate it.

exec: pm.test('status echoed back as INACTIVE', () => pm.expect(status).to.eql('INACTIVE'));

console.warn('PATCH only flips the stored status field - it does NOT stop the client. An INACTIVE client still completes authorize/token/userinfo against this deployment; see the flow-execute inactive-client scenarios.');

request.description:
PATCH /client-mgmt/client/{client_id} - unlike PUT (Update client), this only touches the fields named in the request body; a patch naming other fields leaves status untouched, and a patch naming only status leaves everything else untouched.

Sends Bearer {{admin_token}}, not the Cookie form PMS wants - this route sits behind eSignet's own ScopeMiddleware, which reads Authorization: Bearer <jwt> and checks a configured scope, not the Keycloak-session cookie PMS expects.

Body shown here flips the client to INACTIVE - the operator kill switch for a retired/compromised/offboarded relying party. Re-run with "status": "ACTIVE" to reactivate (idempotent either way). Other patchable fields: clientName, clientNameLangMap, logoUri, redirectUris, userClaims, authContextRefs, grantTypes, clientAuthMethods, additionalConfig, encPublicKey (send JSON null to clear it).

Do NOT run this against {{client_id}} if that variable points at the shared/aged client folder 2 depends on - it flips real state and folder 2's login will start failing for reasons that look unrelated. Prefer running it against {{new_client_id}} from 'Create OIDC client' instead, or override client_id at the request level.

exec: if (code === 'invalid_additional_config') console.error('Check the key names/types - see allowedAdditionalConfigKeys in clientmgmt/validate.go. All three protocol flags here must be JSON booleans.');

console.warn('additionalConfig is a whole-object REPLACE, not a merge: any key not in this body (userinfo_response_type, purpose, allowed_authorization_scopes, ...) is dropped, not preserved. Re-send the full set together if the client already has other additionalConfig keys set.');

console.warn('Neither this response nor GET /client-mgmt/client/{id} echoes additionalConfig back - ClientResponse.APIResponse() only ever returns clientId and status. There is no way to verify PAR/DPoP/PKCE landed through this API; confirm behaviourally (PAR at /oauth2/par, DPoP proof at /oauth2/token, PKCE code_verifier at /oauth2/token) instead.');

request.description:
Turns on the three per-client protocol switches in one PATCH: require_pushed_authorization_requests (PAR), dpop_bound_access_tokens (DPoP), require_pkce (PKCE). All three are plain JSON booleans; set any of them false instead of omitting to turn it back off - omitting the whole additionalConfig key is what leaves it alone, omitting one key INSIDE it does not.

allowedAdditionalConfigKeys also has: userinfo_response_type, id_token_response_type ("JWS"|"JWE"), consent_expire_in_mins (>=10), signup_banner_required, forgot_pwd_link_required, purpose, allowed_authorization_scopes. If the client already has any of these set and you only want to flip PAR/DPoP/PKCE, fetch them first (there is currently no read path for additionalConfig - see the test script) or track what you set at creation, then resend the complete object; a partial body here silently drops the rest.

Same client_id caution as the status patch alongside it: point this at {{new_client_id}}, not the shared client folder 2 relies on.

exec: pm.test('got executionId', () => pm.expect(m, 'no executionId in Location').to.not.be.null);

request.description:
Redirects are deliberately NOT followed - the executionId lives in the Location header.

redirect_uri must exactly match one registered for the client, or eSignet answers 'Invalid redirect URI' before the flow starts.
First view: pick an authentication factor. Offers acr_otp and acr_bio.

Lands on the UIN login-id tab by default.

For a phone or email identity, first POST action 'login_id_mobile' (or login_id_email) to switch tabs. Every tab's submit action is named submit_uin - only nextNode (send_mosip_otp_uin vs send_mosip_otp_mobile) says which identifier kind it actually sends, so submitting a phone on the UIN tab silently sends it as a UIN and IDA rejects it.

exec: if (c === 'IDA-MLC-007') console.error('Usually a client IDA does not know yet - a newly created client needs 20 min to 3 h. Can also be the OTP request rate limit.');
if (c === 'IDA-MLC-009') console.error('IDA could not send to that identifier - try the UIN rather than phone or email.');
console.log('OTP sent - read it from the mock SMTP, put it in the otp variable, then run 2.5');

request.description:
Submits the identifier, which makes IDA send the OTP.

captcha_token can be any non-empty placeholder while the deployment has no captcha validator configured (MOSIP_ESIGNET_CAPTCHA_VALIDATOR_URL unset). With a validator on, only a real reCAPTCHA token passes and this step fails with 'The captcha token could not be verified'.

Note MOSIP_ESIGNET_CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY and _SITE_PROVIDER must stay SET even when the validator is off - the flow definition substitutes them, and unsetting them makes every authorize fail with server_error.

exec: console.error('FET-1005 means IDA refused the credentials: a wrong or expired OTP, or a client IDA has not picked up yet.');
console.log('COMPLETE - consent was already stored for this client, so no prompt.');
if (prompt) { pm.collectionVariables.set('consent_prompt', prompt); console.log('consent prompt stored - run 2.6'); }

request.description:
Set the `otp` variable first - 3 minute validity.

Note username and captcha_token are sent AGAIN alongside otp. Inputs accumulate across the whole flow and every step re-sends all of them. The OTP view declares only `otp`, but submitting just that leaves the auth node with no identity to verify against, and it answers FET-1005 'Invalid credentials provided' as though the code itself were wrong.

exec: // Build an approve-everything decision from the prompt stored by 2.5.
elements: [].concat(p.essential || [], p.optional || []).map(e => ({ name: e.name, approved: true }))
console.log('COMPLETE. The assertion is what the RP posts to /oauth2/auth/callback to obtain its code.');

request.description:
Only needed when 2.5 returned a consent prompt; a client whose consent is already stored goes straight to COMPLETE.

The pre-request script builds consent_decisions from the stored prompt, approving every essential and optional claim. consent_decisions is a JSON *string*, not a nested object - that is what the executor expects.

To test denial, edit the script to set approved:false on the elements you want withheld.
Confirms the base URL is right, and shows supported auth methods and signing algorithms.
Confirms the partner exists and is active.
Check status is PUBLISHED and allowedAuthTypes includes otp and otp-request, or the OTP flow cannot work.
